title: 'Moment to moment' ; Mountie not expected to live, cops IDSt. Albert shooting suspect
article: The Mountie shot in the head during a sudden altercation in a St. Albert Casino Saturday morning is not expected to live.

RCMP K Division Deputy Commissioner Marianne Ryan said Const. David Matthew Wynn, 42, has yet to regain consciousness after being shot in the head Saturday. She said Wynn's care is "moment-to-moment" at this point, and "it is not optimistic that he will survive."
Wynn joined the RCMP in 2009, and is described as "an exceptionally fine officer." He has a wife and three children.
Also shot in the incident was Aux. Const. Derek Walter Bond, 49. Bond has since been released from hospital, but Ryan said his injuries were also severe.
"This was not a case of an officer simply being grazed by a bullet. The bullet narrowly missed vital organs," she said.
Gunfire broke out when Wynn and Bond were trying to arrest Shawn Maxwell Rehn, 34, at the Apex Casino, according to RCMP K Division Assistant Commissioner Marlin DeGrand.
"It was a very, very short and sharp confrontation," he said. "(Rehn) pulled away and two shot were fired."
Mounties say Rehn was found dead soon after Saturday's shooting in an unoccupied private residence in a rural area near St. Albert.

RCMP Commissioner Bob Paulson, who expressed "intense sorrow and sadness for what has happened," said Rehn was "very well known to police," with a "significant accumulation of criminalities and behaviours." Paulson said the fact Rehn was allowed to be walking free is something that needs to be looked at.

When Rehn was 20 years old he was charged with dangerous driving, failing to stop for a police officer and possession of a controlled substance (methamphetamine) after a high-speed pursuit near Evansburg, Alta. His 15-year-old female passenger was also charged with possession of a controlled substance.

Two years later, police charged Rehn and Michael Raymond Harris with weapons-related offences, break and enter and possession of stolen property after a man with a gun was spotted leaving a northwest Edmonton residence in a stolen car.

Police issued a warrant for Rehn in 2005 after a suspect left his identification with the victim of a northside home invasion. Rehn was wanted on charges of break and enter, assault with a weapon and forcible confinement.

Alberta RCMP K Division assistant commissioner Marlin DeGrand said Rhen was found dead by RCMP officers in an unoccupied private residence in a rural area near St. Albert. Officers located him just before noon and tracked him to the house with the intention of arresting him.

Because the body of the suspect was found within a police established containment, the death is being treated as an in-custody death and as a result will be investigated by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT).
Family members of the gravely injured Wynn, who serves with the St. Albert RCMP detachment, were summoned to his bedside by doctors Saturday.
"We are definitely very concerned for his survival", said DeGrand.
The gunfire broke out after Wynn and Bond discovered a car believed to be stolen in the parking lot of the casino.
Sources said the two officers were reviewing surveillance footage inside the casino when they encountered the suspect attempting to leave.
Once spotted, the suspect opened fire, striking Bond in the arm before shooting Wynn in the head and fleeing the scene. An autopsy Monday will determine Rehn's cause of death.
